notes: Run with the skill-creator skill. Each assertion is a failure seen when models build TUIs without the skill (or with an earlier version). Deterministic ones are checked by tuilint and the harness; the rest by a grader reading renders. Add a case whenever the skill misses something in real use: write the miss as an assertion first, make the kit pass it, then edit the skill.

evals.name: dashboard-from-brand-brief
evals.prompt: Build a Bubble Tea TUI for 'tidepool', a CLI that monitors background job queues (queues, workers, failed jobs, retries). Brand: deep sea green #0F5257 and coral #FF6F59, calm but precise, used by on-call engineers at 3am. I need a queue list, a detail view for the selected queue with throughput and failures, a retry confirmation, and an empty state. go run should start it.
evals.expected_output: A Bubble Tea v2 program with a tidepool theme JSON derived from the two hexes, a TUI.md, the harness flags, every state rendered and reviewed, and contact sheets shown.
assertions: imports charm.land/bubbletea/v2 and charm.land/lipgloss/v2 (no v1 imports)
go run ./cmd/<app> with no flags starts tea.NewProgram; -golden -w 80 -h 24 and -w 120 -h 40 exit 0
go test ./... passes in the app's module, the copied internal/ui and cmd/<app> tests included, on the app's own theme (they used to load the kit's themes by path and name)
a themes/tidepool.json exists with dark and light roles derived from #0F5257 and #FF6F59; no hex literals outside the theme package (tuilint code C-HEX passes)
a brand read (read field or .read.md) ties at least 5 expression choices to product traits

palette derive on the brand hexes exits 0 on its first run (its output passes its own check, even for a mid-tone primary such as #2E8B57), and palette check passes the shipped tidepool.json in dark and light with the brand's primary hex kept and no contrastAccept added for an on-colour
diversity shows the theme differs from kit ink on >= 8 axes

diversity was run with kit/themes/ink.json and kit/themes/charm.json among its inputs, so the min-distance rule actually ran (a --baseline name with no matching theme exits 2; it used to be skipped silently)

every role in themes/tidepool.json is #RRGGBB or #RGB with the # (no bare 0F5257, no #RRGGBBAA): theme.Load loads it and palette check exits 0, since Lip Gloss reads a value without # as an ANSI index or no colour
no rendered frame has emoji, library-default pink/purple, or more than one bordered box (tuilint frames passes)
tuilint frames passes on the -light, -ascii and -profile ansi256 renders too, not only dark truecolour (the footer bar, rules and 256-colour fallbacks break there first)
exactly one visible focus in every state, and the focus marker does not shift text
help is generated from key.Bindings; every key shown in a state's help works in that state
retry confirmation names the queue, focuses Cancel by default, and colours the destructive button
empty state says what is missing, why in context, and the one key to fix it
at 120x40 a detail pane or extra section uses the room; at 80x24 it collapses to a summary
the agent rendered PNGs with cellshot and looked at them before replying

palette check passes the shipped theme including its glyphs: every glyph outside ASCII has an ASCII twin (glyphs.ascii or the kit's map) and no two state marks (done/current/todo/pending/partial, radio, check) share one, so a ◐ 'reading' and a ● 'new' never become the same * under -ascii

every dialog has a visible edge at -profile ansi and under NO_COLOR=1, not only in truecolour: a borderless panel one background step up lands on the page's colour there (the kit's dialog: none draws a rule above and below; dialog: rules always has one)
the -ascii renders pass tuilint frames --ascii (F-ASCII): no glyph outside ASCII leaks into an ASCII frame, and a cut footer ends in the full ...

the state ladder (queued, running, retrying, failed, done) draws its marks from the theme's status slots, never literals: in progress is t.G.Partial (◐, ascii ~), not current's ● in another colour, so under NO_COLOR and -ascii every rung keeps its own shape

evals.name: agent-chat-like-crush
evals.prompt: I want a chat UI for my coding agent in the terminal, as nice as Crush but not a copy of it. Brand name 'loom', colours violet #7C5CFF on near-black, but we want it to feel warmer and more editorial than Crush.
evals.expected_output: A chat TUI with messages, tool calls in the Crush grammar, a working animation, an editor, and an identity that differs from the charm study theme.
assertions: tool calls use status glyph + name + main param + k=v options, an indented panel body, and an honest collapsed affordance
one shared animation clock that stops when idle (tick returns nil in idle states)
the working indicator says what is happening (no 'Loading...'/'Thinking...' alone without subject or elapsed time)
diversity: loom differs from the charm study theme on >= 8 axes (not Crush recoloured)
prose is capped at a measure (<= 100 cells) at 200 columns
editor uses a real cursor via tea.View.Cursor
the brand read explains how 'warmer and more editorial' became specific expressions

wordmark generated with wordmark.py (not figlet standard), >= 4 rows for half / >= 5 for shade

frames dumped deterministically via an At(frame)/-frame path; a GIF and a contact sheet were rendered and inspected
a Go test asserts every frame's footprint

evals.expected_output: The same wizard, still on Huh, themed from a brand theme and raised to the idiom: header, stepper, summary with hierarchy, consistent buttons, a sign-in wait with a fallback, before/after contact sheets.
assertions: still built on Huh: no hand-rolled replacement for select, input or confirm
every Huh form and spinner uses the brand theme (kit form theme); no Huh default colours render (#F780E2 spinner, #7571F9/#5A56E0 indigo) [F-DEFAULT, C-HUHTHEME]
not a recolour: at least four of header bar, stepper with done/current/todo glyphs, background step or panel, filled tag, three text levels, boxed footer keys
one button order on every screen: the action first, the negative last (Yes No, Continue Back)
the review step's default is the forward action (Continue), not Edit or Cancel
the selection cursor and an unfocused input's prompt never show the same glyph at once
the step counter advances past review: sign-in and post-save prompts are not all labelled with the last step
the sign-in wait shows the URL to open by hand, elapsed time, and how to cancel
the layout uses the width: no column ends before half the terminal at 120+ columns while the rest is empty, and no value wraps mid-word in a summary
before and after contact sheets were produced and shown

evals.name: init-interview
evals.prompt: /bubbletea-tui init — we're about to build a TUI for our CLI.
evals.expected_output: An interview in short rounds (at most three questions each, every one with a proposed default), then TUI.md with design context and architecture, and a two-line summary of what was assumed.
assertions: explored the repo (README, --help, existing screens, brand assets) before asking anything
asked at most three questions per round, each with a proposed default
wrote TUI.md with product, users and terminals, brand read, theme, screens and states, keys per state, architecture (root model, regions, forms library, async work, harness states), decisions, never
named the forms library and how it is themed (Huh with the kit form theme) in the architecture section
ended by naming the next command (brand or shape) and what it assumed
created no file besides TUI.md (no SPEC.md, PRD or ARCH.md); with no product doc in the repo, TUI.md § Product holds the product facts and the hand-off has no 'Proposed for' line

round 2 confirmed the screen list, each screen with its one-line job, in a question's default (e.g. 'Screens: list — find a job; detail — read its log (recommended)'), instead of inferring the screens silently

evals.name: init-from-existing-spec
evals.prompt: /bubbletea-tui init — SPEC.md describes the TUI we're building. Interview me and write TUI.md.
evals.expected_output: A TUI.md that keeps what SPEC.md decided, catches what it got wrong for a terminal (indistinguishable keys, a global key a text box eats, one accent with three meanings, ambiguous-width state dots), settles which design method governs without skipping the screens question, keeps a visible brand signature and the ◐ glyph, fits every footer in 80 columns, keeps dialogs visible without colour, proposes a first slice of the main loop, and passes tuilint spec.
assertions: no key that terminals without key disambiguation deliver as another key (shift+enter, ctrl+enter, ctrl+m, ctrl+i, ctrl+[, ctrl+backspace …) is advertised in TUI.md's key table without a fallback in the same cell (e.g. `shift+enter/ctrl+j newline`), although SPEC.md asks for Shift+Enter; tuilint spec reports no S-KEYAMBIG

the ctrl+k quick switcher is not a global key in the reply and note states, where a Bubbles textarea deletes to end of line on ctrl+k: it is rebound, or those states bind it explicitly; tuilint spec reports no S-KEYSHADOW for it

the brand read gives each accent hue exactly one meaning, and focus is not drawn in the unread colour, so the inbox cursor row and an unread row look different, although SPEC.md asks amber to mean unread, focus and the active filter

each state dot (● ◐ ○) has an ASCII twin named in TUI.md, and the brand read says how the dots stay width-safe in the inbox's state column (they are East Asian Width ambiguous); tuilint spec reports no S-GLYPHWIDTH
TUI.md's architecture half says one fixtures file feeds both the harness (-state, -out) and the tests, and names a fake for each external service (the forge CLI and the Beacon API)
noticed that SPEC.md routes screen design to 'the Grainline method', asked which method governs the screens before writing TUI.md, and recorded the answer with its reason in TUI.md § Decisions
TUI.md proposes a first slice: the smallest milestone that renders the core screens (inbox, thread, reply) on fixtures before any integration, with the rest of the v1 list ordered after it

the project ends with a way for a fresh clone to get the skill back: skills-lock.json plus the .claude/skills link committed (restored with npx skills experimental_install), or .agents/skills/ committed, as SKILL.md Setup says
TUI.md names one hero animation for the long-running action (the AI summary or a source refresh), drawn from the brand motif and at most 30 cells wide, and says nothing moves while idle
TUI.md's architecture half names the largest realistic data (the 20,000-line diff, a thread of hundreds of comments) and how it stays fast: a virtual list or a render cache with its key
TUI.md says how focus, selection and errors stay visible under -profile ascii and lists the colour profiles it supports (truecolor, 256, 16, none)
the key table has a partial state for the inbox (one of Forge, Beacon or mail failed while the others loaded), besides its empty, loading and error states

TUI.md is the only file init created or changed (apart from the skill install files): SPEC.md is untouched, its product changes from the interview are listed in the hand-off as a proposed edit, and no layout, key, colour or screen detail was written outside TUI.md

round 2 confirmed the screen list, each screen with its job, in a question's default, although the Grainline conflict also needed a question: the conflict got its own short round or replaced a lower-value question, never the screens one, and the flows SPEC.md describes outside § Screens (morning triage with bulk mark-done and snooze, acknowledging a Beacon page from anywhere) appear in that list or are deferred by name
the brand read's remember line names a move the TUI draws on every screen (the state-dot column, a rule, a gutter, a layout move), not a quality of the content such as 'reads like a well-set page'
the ● ◐ ○ ✓ state ladder keeps ◐: it has an ASCII twin and sits in a 2-cell column, and is not dropped or replaced by plain text for being ambiguous-width

no state's footer keys overflow the 80-column footer: a state with more actions than fit (the inbox) marks its footer (bold keys, or ‖ after them), keeping its main actions and its way out in it and the rest reachable from ? help; tuilint spec reports no S-FOOTER

TUI.md's colour line says what separates dialogs and overlays from the page where the background step is gone (16 colours, NO_COLOR, -profile ascii), e.g. a hairline rule or border, although SPEC.md asks for borderless filled panels
the First slice is the main loop's 2–3 screens (inbox, thread, reply) with every state of those on fixtures, not every state of every screen; note, the quick switcher and the rest come after it
